title: Implementing motion with Material Design | Google Design Tutorials
summary: Sharon Harris (motion designer, Material team) presents the Material motion system as four reusable transition patterns, each tied to a kind of relationship between two screens: container transform, shared axis, fade-through and fade. Every pattern is shown in slow motion on four phone mock-ups, then wired up on Android; she closes with how to customise duration, easing and motion path, and with timeline-style motion specs that let designers hand exact timings to engineers.

insights.insight: Container transform: when one element (a card) becomes the next screen (its detail page), animate that same container growing into the new layout so the eye never loses it. The user reads the detail page as 'the card, opened', not as a new place. Pick the pattern by the relationship: strong parent/child link = container transform.
insights.quote: This pattern creates a visible connection between two UI elements.
insights.visual: Slow-motion demo on four phones mid-transition: a FAB on a calendar is growing into a white form sheet, an inbox row is expanding into the email, an album tile has grown into the full player. The sheet and the row are caught half-way, still showing their origin.

insights.insight: Shared axis: for steps of a sequence (a setup flow, Next / Back), outgoing and incoming content slide together along ONE axis (x for steps, y for scroll-like, z for parent/child) and cross-fade. Moving in the same direction tells the user the two screens are neighbours in one space, and the Back gesture runs the same motion in reverse ('forward' flag sets the direction).
insights.quote: By moving in the same direction, elements are perceived to be related
insights.visual: Three phones in slow motion: a 'Streamline your courses' setup step with BACK / NEXT buttons, a recipe step list and a photo viewer, each caught while the old content slides out and fades as the new one slides in on the same axis.

insights.insight: Fade-through: when two destinations are NOT spatially related (bottom-nav tabs), do not slide them, because a slide falsely promises you can swipe between them. Fade the old content out, then fade/scale the new one in. Motion direction is a promise about the app's map, so only use spatial motion where the space is real.
insights.quote: doesn't mislead users into thinking that they can swipe horizontally
insights.visual: Three phones (library grid, settings list, inbox) at the exact middle of a fade-through: both the outgoing and incoming content are washed out to near-white, no lateral movement.

insights.insight: Fade for things that appear over the current screen (dialogs, menus, snackbars, FAB): entering = a quick fade plus a subtle scale-up, exiting = a plain, faster fade out. Overlays should not travel across the screen; they bloom in place and leave quietly.
insights.visual: Four phones: a date-picker dialog over a dimmed screen, an overflow menu dropping from the toolbar, a snackbar at the bottom of an inbox, and a FAB on a calendar, labelled 'Slow motion'.

insights.insight: The patterns are functional defaults; style comes from duration, easing and motion path. Swapping the straight path of a container transform for an arc makes the same transition more emphasised and dramatic, a cheap way to give a hero moment more character without inventing a new pattern.
insights.quote: using an Arc motion path creates a more emphasized and dramatic style
insights.visual: Container open spec for the album card (see next insight): the same container transform the arc path would be applied to.

insights.insight: Spec motion as a timeline, not a GIF. The container-open spec shown runs 300 ms in total: the container animates (scales to width, pinned to top) over the full 0-300 ms, the background scales down to 80% over the same span, the scrim fades in during the first ~100 ms, and the incoming elements fade in only in a short window around 75-150 ms. Layered, offset sub-animations inside one short duration are what make it read as one smooth move.
insights.visual: Interactive 'Direct' spec: the album player on the left and a 'CONTAINER OPEN / CONTAINER CLOSE' timeline on the right with bars for Opacity (incoming elements), Container animates, Scale (background to 80%) and Opacity (scrim), a frames/ms ruler 0-300 ms and the playhead at 277/300 ms.

apply_to_wael: Use a horizontal shared-axis transition for the linear onboarding steps (welcome -> level -> subject -> question 1-3): outgoing and incoming panels slide together and cross-fade, about 300 ms. Because the app is Arabic RTL, 'forward' means the new step enters from the LEFT and the old one leaves to the right; Back plays the exact reverse.

Use a container transform when the chosen subject card becomes the game screen: the tapped subject badge/card grows into the game frame (or the game's header) so the player sees they are 'inside' that subject. Same for the result card expanding into the account-creation sheet.

Show the result and any hint/confirm popups with the fade pattern (quick fade + slight scale-up from ~0.92, fast plain fade out), not slides; and use fade-through only where two steps have no spatial link (e.g. account form -> town map if the camera move is not available).

Write each transition as a small timeline before coding (total ~300 ms; background scale/blur over the full span, scrim in the first third, new content fading in a short mid window) so the CSS/JS keyframes of the whole first-launch flow share one rhythm.
